answer.rationale: memory_73 (targeted promotional pricing for SMB segments) is least supported for the sustainable long-term qualified revenue objective because it explicitly targets price-sensitive segments and relies on promotional discounting. While it reports acquisition and revenue lift, discounting strategies risk eroding unit economics, attracting low-LTV cohorts, and creating margin pressure—all potentially undermining sustainability. The memory lacks data on cohort retention, customer lifetime value, or whether lifted revenue persists post-promotion. memory_44 (enterprise sales-assisted flows) ranks highest: it directly addresses qualified revenue through demonstrated pipeline quality improvement, and enterprise segments typically deliver higher LTV and sustainability. memory_31, memory_86, and memory_91 all support activation and onboarding—foundational to long-term value—with no mention of cannibalization or churn harm. memory_57 (referral incentives) rates moderate-to-good: it adds qualified revenue from established customers (retention signal) without measured retention damage, though 'no measurable harm' is weaker than affirmative LTV evidence.
